## Claims
- [proved] Assuming the accepted graded basis \(Q=\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^a}\mathbb Z\,e_\rho\), with \(\deg e_\rho=ij+|\rho|\), one has
  \[
  H_Q(z)=z^{ij}\sum_{\rho\subseteq b^a}z^{|\rho|}
  =z^{ij}\binom{a+b}{a}_z.
  \]
- [proved] The formula
  \[
  \rho^\vee=(b-\rho_a,\ldots,b-\rho_1)
  \]
  is an involution on partitions in \(b^a\) and satisfies
  \[
  |\rho^\vee|=ab-|\rho|.
  \]
- [proved] The integral bilinear form
  \[
  \langle e_\rho,e_\sigma\rangle=\delta_{\sigma,\rho^\vee}
  \]
  is a perfect degree-complement pairing
  \[
  Q_d\times Q_{\,2ij+ab-d}\longrightarrow\mathbb Z.
  \]

## Strategy
Write
\[
F_{a,b}(z):=\sum_{\rho\subseteq b^a}z^{|\rho|}.
\]
Splitting partitions according as \(\rho_1<b\) or \(\rho_1=b\), and removing the first row in the latter case, gives
\[
F_{a,b}(z)=F_{a,b-1}(z)+z^bF_{a-1,b}(z),
\qquad F_{0,b}=F_{a,0}=1.
\]
The Gaussian binomial
\[
\binom{a+b}{a}_z
=\prod_{t=1}^{a}\frac{1-z^{b+t}}{1-z^t}
\]
satisfies the same recurrence and boundary conditions. Hence
\[
F_{a,b}(z)=\binom{a+b}{a}_z.
\]
Summing the degrees of the accepted basis gives the Hilbert-series formula.

For the pairing, \((\rho^\vee)^\vee=\rho\), so its matrix in the basis \(\{e_\rho\}\) is a permutation matrix over \(\mathbb Z\); hence it is unimodular and perfect. Since
\[
\deg e_\rho+\deg e_{\rho^\vee}
=(ij+|\rho|)+(ij+ab-|\rho|)=2ij+ab,
\]
it has the asserted complementary degrees.

The requested target is established, conditional only on the accepted graded-basis statement.

## Gaps
None under that accepted-basis hypothesis.
